# ezghcloud_access_point (Resource)

An application's entry into a file system: a folder as its root and, optionally, a fixed POSIX user. Destroying it removes the entry, never the files.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ezghcloud_access_point" "wp_content" {
  project_id     = var.project_id
  file_system_id = ezghcloud_file_system.shared.id
  name           = "wp-content"

  root_directory = {
    path = "/wordpress/wp-content"
    creation_info = {
      owner_uid   = 33
      owner_gid   = 33
      permissions = "755"
    }
  }

  posix_user = {
    uid = 33
    gid = 33
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `file_system_id` (String) File system (fsy_) it exposes. Changing it replaces the access point.
- `name` (String) Name, 1 to 100 characters.
- `project_id` (String) Project identifier. Changing it replaces the access point.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Optional description; null clears it.
- `posix_user` (Attributes) User and group every request through the access point runs as, whatever the client sends. Without it, the file system's root_squash applies. Any change replaces the access point. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--posix_user))
- `root_directory` (Attributes) Folder clients see as the root when they mount the access point. Defaults to the file system's root. Any change replaces the access point. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--root_directory))
- `tags` (Map of String) Resource tags.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Access point ID (fap_).
- `organization_id` (String) Organization managed by the configured provider.
- `resource_name` (String) IAM resource name.
- `status` (String) What the access point is doing: creating, available, deleting or failed.

<a id="nestedatt--posix_user"></a>
### Nested Schema for `posix_user`

Required:

- `gid` (Number) Group ID.
- `uid` (Number) User ID.

Optional:

- `secondary_gids` (List of Number) Not supported: leave it unset or []. Always [] in state.


<a id="nestedatt--root_directory"></a>
### Nested Schema for `root_directory`

Optional:

- `creation_info` (Attributes) Owner and mode to create path with when it doesn't exist. Without it, a missing path fails the create. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--root_directory--creation_info))
- `path` (String) Absolute, normalized path inside the file system, such as /wordpress/wp-content.

<a id="nestedatt--root_directory--creation_info"></a>
### Nested Schema for `root_directory.creation_info`

Required:

- `owner_gid` (Number) Owner group ID.
- `owner_uid` (Number) Owner user ID.
- `permissions` (String) Octal mode, such as 755.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Replace identifiers with values from your organization.
terraform import ezghcloud_access_point.example 'ORGANIZATION_ID/PROJECT_ID/RESOURCE_ID'
```
